children: A firm set up by Indonesia to monitor the country's commodity exports has proposed a charge of 0.5% of the export sales value of palm oil, an official with the Indonesia Palm Oil Association (GAPKI) said on Thursday.
Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI) held a briefing with GAPKI and other palm oil industry groups on Wednesday, GAPKI official Yustinus Lambang Setyo Putro said
DSI was established to verify export transactions of Indonesia's key palm oil, coal and ferronickel commodities in order to improve state oversight
DSI plans to launch its digital platform, which will collect a variety of data relating to contracts, shipment volumes and prices, in December
It aims to start collecting the verification fees from January 1
On top of the 0.5% fee, DSI also plans to charge 2.5 million rupiah ($136.54) for each contract uploaded by exporters to the platform, Yustinus said

GAPKI is calculating the size of the impact the additional fees would have on palm oil farmers and companies, Yustinus said, adding that the implementation of a commodity exchange planned for next year would also incur expenses
A DSI spokesperson said she could not immediately comment
